title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for bond and end-of-lease cleaning
audience: Owners of bond and end-of-lease cleaning businesses, including solo operators, who quote move-out cleans for tenants, agents and property managers.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for an end-of-lease clean
instruction.body: 'I do bond cleans' is a service. 'I clean to the agreed list, send photos at handover, and return within a set window to redo any listed item that is missed' is an offer. The agent or tenant buys a clean that matches the list they agreed, and the certainty that the list has been checked. You do not sell a bond refund. In Victoria, a landlord who claims part of the bond must go through VCAT (Tenants Victoria, 2024). Other states' processes were not checked. Pass rates for bond cleans were not found in the research, so do not promise one.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a bond clean offer
instruction.body: Set the outcome (the agreed list, such as rooms, kitchen, bathrooms, oven and fridge), the time frame (on-site time measured on past move-outs of the same size), what the agent or tenant must provide (access, keys, power and water on, the entry condition report if one exists), the certainty you give (photos at handover, a signed checklist) and the risk you carry (a return visit). A written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). WA guidance says a quote should set out the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish (WA only).

instruction.heading: Tiers for a move-out
instruction.body: Use a good-better-best layout: a standard move-out to the agreed list, a plus level that adds oven and fridge interiors, and a deep level that adds windows or other items as separate lines. Jobber shows house cleaning as one trade example of stepped packages (published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). Keep each optional item on its own line, so the agent can see what has been added and what it costs.

instruction.heading: Show one total, and check the rule before you quote
instruction.body: Show one total including GST and say whether GST is included (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024; WA guidance for WA). In Victoria, for agreements signed from 29 March 2021, a provider cannot ask a renter to get professional cleaning unless the property must be returned to its starting state or needs professional cleaning (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 14 October 2026). Check the agent's request against that test before you quote. The research did not check the rules for other states.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and the fix-first return visit
instruction.body: Offer a return visit to fix listed items that were missed. Under the consumer guarantees a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria's guidance, 13 October 2023; a Victorian page, so check your state's consumer agency). That page sets no fix window, so set and test your own. A 'no refunds' line does not override service rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Do not promise a bond refund, a pass or any landlord's outcome.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence that an agent or tenant would repeat, tied to the agreed list.
Ask for the agent's cleaning list and the entry condition report, if they exist, before quoting.
Check whether the property must be returned to its starting state, using the Victorian rule where it applies.
Measure on-site time for past move-outs of each size, and set the tiers from that record.
List each optional item as its own line, and state the exclusions.
Decide the return-visit window, check it against your calendar, then price the quote and show one total with GST stated.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A Melbourne agent asks a bond cleaner for a quote on a two-bedroom apartment being vacated. The agent wants a clean that will be ready for the next tenant. No list has been agreed, and the cleaner has been losing jobs to a lower per-room quote.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer, and decide what the quote must contain before it is sent.
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner first asks for the entry condition report and the agent's list, because the Victorian rule depends on whether the property must be returned to its starting state. The offer is a fixed-scope move-out to that list, with photos at handover, the oven and fridge interiors as separate optional lines, and a return visit within a set window for any listed item that is missed. The cleaner does not promise a bond refund or a pass, because the outcome depends on the landlord's claim and any VCAT process, and pass rates were not researched. The Beyond Pricing band for a two-bedroom move-out is $160 to $220 (28 October 2026). That band is short-stay fee data used as a proxy, so it is a check, not a bond price. The quote states the scope its price rests on.

commonErrors.error: Promising a bond refund or a pass.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the clean to the agreed list and the return visit, which are what you control.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a professional clean as required when the Victorian rule does not require it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the renting rule before quoting, and agree a scope the agent can confirm in writing.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no written list or exclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: Attach the agent's list, or your own list with photos, and state what is excluded.

commonErrors.error: Using the short-stay fee table as a bond price without saying so.
commonErrors.prevention: Label the proxy and its source. Bond-specific pricing was not found in the research.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant a cleaning licence, registration or insurance. Licence and insurance rules for bond cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for the state where the property is.

Victoria only: the renting rules on professional cleaning apply to agreements signed from 29 March 2021 (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 14 October 2026). Other states' tenancy rules were not checked, so check the rules where the property is.
Price display: show the total including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). Consumer guarantees for services cannot be removed by contract (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Sell a clean to a written list, with a return visit. Never sell a guaranteed bond outcome.
In Victoria, check the professional-cleaning rule before quoting. Other states need their own check.
Gaps: bond-specific pricing, agent channels and pass rates were not sourced.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a bond clean offer does the agent or tenant buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
A clean to a written list, with a return visit

knowledgeChecks.question: An agent in Victoria asks for a professional clean. What is the first thing to check?
options: Whether the agent has a favourite cleaner
Whether the property must be returned to its starting state or needs professional cleaning under the renting rules
Whether the price is lower than the short-stay table

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a bond clean quote not promise a refund of the bond?
options: Refunds are always guaranteed by law
The cleaner does not control the landlord's claim process

sourceReferences: WA Consumer Protection, 'Ask us: Estimates and quotes', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/publications/ask-us-estimates-and-quotes, last updated 18 November 2024. Western Australia only. Supports: a quote is a fixed price and an estimate can move; extra work needs the customer's permission; a written quote should state the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish.

business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: an optional warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees; a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: show the total including GST and say whether GST is included; a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent; extra work needs written approval.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Victoria. Supports: a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; the page sets no fix-window length.

Consumer Affairs Victoria, 'Condition reports', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/renting/rent-bond-bills-and-condition-reports/condition-reports, last updated 14 October 2026. Victoria. Supports: for agreements from 29 March 2021 a provider cannot ask renters to get professional cleaning unless the property must be returned to its starting state or needs professional cleaning; exit condition report within 10 days; renter present or given a reasonable opportunity; evidence at least 3 business days before a claim.

Tenants Victoria, 'Bonds factsheet', https://tenantsvic.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Factsheet-Bonds.pdf, dated 2024 in the research file (URL path shows August 2024). Victoria; community legal centre. Supports: a landlord claiming part of the bond must go through VCAT; if no VCAT application disputes the claim within 14 days, the bond is repaid as requested.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source, updated after 2022. Supports: stepped packages where each higher level adds something the customer can see; house cleaning is one trade example.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Notes: the $160 to $220 band is a vendor proxy from short-stay fee data, not a bond price. The Victorian rules are Victoria only. The Tenants Victoria factsheet is dated 2024 in the research file; the URL path shows August 2024.
